questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real headline advantage of InfiniBand NDR over modern Ethernet for training clusters?
options: Raw per-port bandwidth, since Ethernet can never exceed 100 Gb/s
Lower latency and natively lossless behavior, not raw bandwidth
InfiniBand is always cheaper to deploy
InfiniBand doesn't require any switches
questions.explain: Modern 400GbE Ethernet can match InfiniBand's port bandwidth. The real difference is InfiniBand's much lower latency (around 1 microsecond or less) and its natively lossless, credit-based fabric.

questions.q: What does GPUDirect RDMA allow that plain RDMA does not?
options: It allows a NIC to write directly into or out of GPU memory, skipping host (CPU) RAM entirely
It allows training without any network at all
It eliminates the need for NCCL
It only works over Ethernet, never InfiniBand
questions.explain: Plain RDMA bypasses the CPU and OS kernel network stack to transfer between machine memories, but GPUDirect RDMA goes further, writing directly into or out of GPU memory so data never has to be staged through host RAM.

questions.q: Why does a single dropped packet matter more during a ring AllReduce than during typical web traffic?
options: Dropped packets never happen during AllReduce
Because ring AllReduce is fully synchronous — every GPU in the ring stalls waiting for the retransmission before any of them can proceed
Because web traffic uses InfiniBand too
Because AllReduce doesn't use any network protocol
questions.explain: Since every GPU in a ring AllReduce depends on receiving data from its neighbor before it can proceed, a single dropped packet anywhere in the ring stalls the entire collective until it's retransmitted — unlike typical traffic where a retransmission affects only one flow.

questions.q: What mechanism does InfiniBand use natively to avoid packet loss from congestion?
options: TCP retransmission
Credit-based flow control, where a sender only transmits once the receiver confirms buffer space is available
Random packet dropping to signal congestion
Priority Flow Control (PFC) and ECN
questions.explain: InfiniBand natively uses credit-based flow control to avoid congestion-based drops. PFC and ECN are the mechanisms Ethernet uses (via RoCEv2) to approximate this same lossless behavior, but they require careful configuration.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when might Ethernet be a reasonable choice instead of InfiniBand?
options: Never — InfiniBand is always strictly better for any workload
For workloads with less synchronous, less latency-sensitive traffic, or where an organization already has strong Ethernet/RoCEv2 operational expertise
Only when training models smaller than 1 billion parameters
Only for inference, never for any kind of training
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as a tradeoff based on traffic pattern and organizational expertise, not an absolute rule — Ethernet with RoCEv2 is a legitimate, often cheaper choice for workloads that don't hit InfiniBand's specific strengths as hard as collective-heavy LLM training does.
